threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You catch yourself looking for a bus after 8pm instead of getting used to the night buses; that's a sure sign you're still adjusting.
Last night on the 36, a man serenaded the entire bus with a ukulele rendition of 'Wonderwall.' The driver just nodded along, made the midnight ride somehow magical.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy juggling in front of Rewe while waiting for the Bus M41, I realized this place has its own rhythm.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a spontaneous dance party pop up in the middle of a laundromat, complete with funky beats and locals rocking their laundry.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Only locals know to carry a snack in their bag for long BART delays—nothing worse than being stuck with empty stomach while waiting for those trains.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Watched a guy in a full suit casually hop on the 31, balancing a saxophone under one arm and a cup of coffee in the other. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is just about the plazas, but it’s the small alleys where you find the cafés with the best croissants—like those hidden by Carrer de Verdi.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still ask for pa amb tomàquet with a fork and knife, while locals just grab it with their hands.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You can spot the newbies—clutching their phones looking lost at every bus stop, expecting the tube to be an option.
Saw a bloke on the N133 serenading the driver with an old Marvin Gaye hit. Smooth moves, but the rest of us just wanted to sleep.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I found a tiny artisan bakery hidden in a back alley, with the scent of fresh bread slicing through the usual chaos. Pure Neukölln magic.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you find a Späti that sells beer and organic veggies side by side. It's like a late-night farmer's market with a party twist.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: Locals know to avoid 16th and Mission during rush hour; the bus delays there are a rite of passage, not just a pain.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy playing classical guitar on the 19 bus, while a toddler danced next to him. Muni magic, even amidst the chaos of delays.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists always think they can find true 'cava' in every bar. But the real stuff’s hidden in family-run shops, not on the main strip.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: They’re the ones still fumbling around with the T10 card machines, staring at the screens like it’s a spaceship control panel.
